the sampling frequency of the underrepresented Medium and Hard samples. The strategy-specificγvalues were
determined before model fine-tuning based on the degree of dataset imbalance and were applied consistently
across all model configurations.

The performance of all model configurations and their fine-tuned variants was evaluated using the F1 score. 21
Predicted and reference instances were matched using an IoU threshold of 0.5. The F1 score was computed for
each test patch and then averaged across all test patches. It was calculated as:
F1 = 2TP
2TP + FP + FN,
where TP, FP, and FN denote true-positive, false-positive, and false-negative nuclei instances, respectively.
The F1 score was used as the primary evaluation metric because it jointly accounts for false-positive and false-
negative predictions.

by
combining Medium and Hard annotations. Cellpose 3.0 achieved its highest F1 score using the complete Easy plus
Medium plus Hard dataset. In contrast, Hard-only fine-tuning was optimal for Cellpose-DINO and LSP-DETR.
Overall, seven of the nine best-performing strategies included the newly annotated Medium data. Although
Easy + Hard fine-tuning improved performance over the corresponding baseline for eight of the nine model
configurations, it was not the optimal strategy for any model once Medium-containing strategies were included
in the comparison. These results indicate that the newly annotated Medium cases provided complementary
kidney-specific supervision beyond the previously available Easy and Hard data, although the optimal data
composition remained model dependent.

We observed substantial differences in the magnitude of improvement across models. StarDist showed the
largest absolute gain, increasing from 0.7380 to 0.8332 with Medium-only fine-tuning, corresponding to an
improvement of 0.0952. Cellpose-SAM showed the second-largest gain of 0.0841. Cellpose 3.0 and Cellpose-
DINO improved by 0.0630 and 0.0625, respectively. We also observed smaller but consistent gains for CellViT
[HIPT-256], LSP-DETR, CellViT++ [Virchow], CellViT [SAM-H], and PathoSAM. These results show that the
effect of human-in-the-loop data enrichment varied according to the model configuration and its baseline.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline F1 gains are measured on a fixed 185-patch expert-annotated hold-out set explicitly excluded from training, validation, pseudo-label generation, and data enrichment.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Instance-level F1 at IoU 0.5 against expert ground-truth annotations on the independent 185-patch hold-out test set.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Fine-tuning supervision from Easy pseudo-labels and expert Medium/Hard annotations via task segmentation loss with AdamW.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims that Medium annotations offer complementary supervision and that optimal fine-tuning compositions are model-dependent are directly backed by the reported benchmark metrics and qualitative comparisons.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation systematically assesses 63 fine-tuning experiments on an independent hold-out test set of 185 expert-annotated kidney pathology patches using instance-level F1 score at IoU 0.5, with clear baseline comparisons.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations were performed on a separate, fixed hold-out test set of 185 expert-annotated patches completely excluded from training, validation, and pseudo-label selection.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Instance-level F1 score computed at an IoU threshold of 0.5 against an independent hold-out test set of 185 expert-annotated kidney pathology patches.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Fine-tuning was supervised on varying mixtures of foundation-model pseudo-labels (Easy) and expert manual ground-truth annotations (Medium and Hard) using task segmentation loss via AdamW.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently acknowledge limitations, including restriction to renal pathology, a single 185-patch hold-out test set, predefined non-tuned oversampling weights, and reliance on single training runs without stochastic variance bounds.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the curation of Easy pseudo-labels, Hard failure annotations, and 860 newly annotated Medium patches, alongside weighted oversampling to balance source contributions during fine-tuning across nine distinct model architectures.
primary.quality_rationale: The study offers a well-scoped, rigorously conducted benchmark addressing an established open question regarding human-in-the-loop data efficiency in computational pathology, providing reproducible experimental details and clear boundaries.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper provides an empirical evaluation and fine-tuning study investigating whether adding expert annotations of intermediate-difficulty ('Medium') renal pathology patches improves cell nuclei instance segmentation across nine foundation model configurations under seven adaptation data mixtures.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study offers a well-scoped, rigorously conducted benchmark addressing an established open question regarding human-in-the-loop data efficiency in computational pathology, providing reproducible experimental details and clear boundaries.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently acknowledge limitations, including restriction to renal pathology, a single 185-patch hold-out test set, predefined non-tuned oversampling weights, and reliance on single training runs without stochastic variance bounds.
